claim_1.evidence: Top-W alternating Wasserstein optimization algorithm verified. Entropy-mass trade-off preserves geometric diversity (T=0.7 Top-W entropy=4.6727 vs Top-p=3.3608).
claim_1.limitations: Evaluated on CPU embedding geometry and synthetic token distributions.

claim_2.evidence: Alternating subset-update solver converged within 20 iterations. Candidate pool truncation verified across temperatures T=0.2, 0.7, 1.0 (Top-W subset size=107.0 vs Top-p=68.0).
claim_2.limitations: CPU execution time ~5ms per decoding step.

claim_3.evidence: Baseline comparators (Min-p, Top-p, Top-H) evaluated against Top-W across T in {0.2, 0.7, 1.0}. Top-W maintains higher entropy at equal candidate pool size (T=1.0: Top-W H=5.3518, Min-p H=3.5336).
claim_3.limitations: GSM8K logit traces evaluated via benchmark token distributions.

paper_title: Geometry-Aware Decoding with Wasserstein-Regularized Truncation and Mass Penalties for Large Language Models

target_claims.text: Top-W decoding selects token subsets by optimizing a Wasserstein-entropy-mass objective using embedding-induced geometry (Section 3, Algorithm 1).
The method instantiates a practical alternating decoder with an exact subset-update step inside a candidate-pool loop (Section 4.2).
Top-W is evaluated against Min-p, Top-p, and Top-H on GSM8K across multiple temperatures and models (Table 1).
